**2B.7 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Overall read: **mostly negative**. I found one genuine diplomatic example around Rohingya repatriation, but the main 2024 crisis - the student protests - did **not** produce credible evidence that Hasina chose ceasefires, compromise, lawful settlement, or reconciliation when a peaceful route was available.

**Accepted claims**

- **PM Hasina reiterates call to China to help repatriate Rohingyas to Myanmar**
  - **Publisher:** TBS News / UNB
  - **Date:** July 10, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar-895921
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina publicly pushed a diplomatic track for Rohingya repatriation through talks with Myanmar and support from China. This is the clearest 2024 example of pursuing a peaceful settlement channel when available.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.1, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh said it would not admit more Rohingya because supporting the existing population threatened its own security**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** February 7, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-will-not-let-in-any-more-rohingya-refugees-minister/1958020/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh justified its refusal to take more Rohingya as a security necessity. This is defensive diplomacy rather than conflict escalation, though it is not a ceasefire or reconciliation case.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh ramps up border vigilance as thousands of Rohingya flee Myanmar**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** September 11, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-ramps-up-border-vigilance-as-thousands-of-rohingya-flee-myanmar/2262488/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Bangladesh tightened border vigilance amid new refugee flows from Myanmar. This is a defensive security move, not evidence of war-making or rejection of negotiation.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.3, 1B.1

- **Student killed amid violent anti-quota protests in Bangladesh**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** July 16, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/student-killed-amid-violent-anti-quota-protests-in-bangladesh/2177010/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that protests continued after Hasina refused to meet student demands, even though the Supreme Court had already suspended the quota order. This shows a credible lawful/de-escalatory path existed, but Hasina did not take it as the first response.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.8

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / Investing.com
  - **Date:** July 22, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-calm-a-day-after-top-court-scrapped-some-job-quotas-3528153
  - **Claim-level summary:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed opponents for the violence instead of moving toward compromise or a durable settlement. That is strong evidence against using negotiation as the preferred option.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** July 20, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters described internet/text shutdowns and a nationwide curfew as the government escalated. This is the opposite of ceasefire or confidence-building behavior.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigns, interim government to be formed**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint
  - **Date:** August 5, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-resigns-interim-government-to-be-formed/2208572/
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported Hasina fled after the crisis peaked and an interim government would be formed. The crisis resolved through collapse, not through negotiated reconciliation.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July ‘killings and vandalism’**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** August 13, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/
  - **Claim-level summary:** After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into killings and vandalism. This is a post-hoc accountability signal, but it is not evidence that she pursued reconciliation or a ceasefire when it could have mattered.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.7, 1B.8

**Search gap**

- I searched for 2024 evidence of ceasefires, peace talks, confidence-building measures, lawful settlements, and reconciliation.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Hasina used those tools in the student-protest crisis.
- Bangladesh did not have a conventional interstate war in 2024, so the most relevant peace-settlement test case was domestic, and the record there is strongly coercive.

**Bottom line**

- Best-supported conclusion: **Hasina only showed limited diplomatic behavior in 2024, and she did not credibly pursue ceasefire-like compromise or reconciliation when peaceful alternatives existed.**
